name: お好み焼 鉄板焼 やつなみ (Okonomiyaki Teppanyaki Yatsunami)

claims.text: All food is cooked on a single shared teppan griddle alongside wheat-batter okonomiyaki and wheat noodles, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
The restaurant uses Otafuku okonomiyaki sauce, which is wheat-based and not gluten-free.
The griddle is continuously used for pork, beef, oysters and egg, so any item would share surfaces with animal products.

name: お好み焼 よっちゃん (Okonomiyaki Yocchan)

claims.text: Single shared teppan griddle on which wheat-based okonomiyaki and noodles are cooked together; no separation documented.
Finished with okonomiyaki/Carp brand sauce (Mouri Brewing), which is wheat-containing and not gluten-free.
All okonomiyaki are made with pork and egg as standard and cooked on a shared griddle with other meat and seafood toppings.

name: おにぎり屋 三兎 (Onigiriya Santo)

claims.text: Fillings include koji-seasoned and braised items (e.g., braised anago) and savory varieties that typically rely on wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free seasoning is documented.
The menu is built around fish and seafood (anago, oyster, salmon, ikura, tuna), so plant-based items would be prepared in the same fish-handling space.
Onigiri are hand-made to order with the nori provided separately, so customers can see the simple components and add the seaweed themselves.

name: お食事処 快心友 (Oshokujidokoro Kaishin'yu)

claims.text: The signature anago-don uses a house-made sweet tare (sauce); eel-style tare is conventionally based on wheat-containing soy sauce and mirin. No gluten-free preparation is documented.
Menu is centered on conger eel and oysters with fish-cake (kamaboko) sides; no plant-based options are documented, so cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.

name: お食事処 新京本店 (Oshokujidokoro Shinkyo Honten)

claims.text: Home-style braised side dishes and dashi-based dishes are seasoned with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat.
The signature curry soup contains beef and beef tendon and a fish-based dashi (kombu, iriko, katsuo), so it is not suitable for vegans or vegetarians.

name: おやつカフェ ユルム。 (Oyatsu Cafe Yurumu)

claims.text: The kitchen bakes with domestic wheat flour, so the environment is not gluten-free and cross-contact with wheat is inherent.
The whole product line is made without eggs, dairy, or white sugar, so the kitchen does not handle those animal ingredients alongside the baked goods.

The owner started baking precisely because of her own allergy (severe atopic dermatitis) and built the shop around requests from other allergy-sufferers, so she is highly attuned to egg/dairy/white-sugar avoidance.
Fully egg-free, dairy-free and white-sugar-free baking using beet sugar, brown rice malt syrup and soy milk — a reliable vegan-friendly sweets stop.
Prioritizes domestic, organic and pesticide-free ingredients where possible, such as organic strawberries for smoothies.

name: パルコ デッラ パーチェ (PARCO della PACE)

claims.text: This is a wheat-flour wood-fired pizzeria with no gluten-free crust or menu documented; flour is used openly in an open kitchen, so airborne and surface gluten cross-contact should be assumed.

A reviewer observed staff using the same pizza cutter for meat and vegetarian pizzas, and not washing hands between handling meat and making the vegetarian pizza. Strict vegans should request fresh utensils and prep.
The owner provided a handwritten English ingredient list to confirm a dessert was free of animal products, indicating willingness to verify ingredients on request.
Vegan and vegetarian pizzas are clearly marked on the menu with hand-drawn icons and signage, and a separate English vegetarian/vegan menu is available.
Four dedicated vegan pizzas plus vegan dessert options, with the ability to customize a pizza from listed toppings.

name: ピース ブルバード (Peace Blvd)

claims.text: Set meals feature Japanese dishes such as simmered mackerel and white-miso-dressed vegetables, which in standard Japanese cooking use soy sauce and miso that typically contain wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is documented.
The cafe centers on rice and onigiri made from high-grade Okuizumo Nita-mai, and plain salted rice balls are naturally gluten-free even though the surrounding set components are not.
